---
title: "Usage"
---

## Enable modules

Add to `~/.bashrc` (replace `~/hpc` with your install directory):

```bash
source ~/hpc/lmod/9.5/init/bash
module use ~/hpc/modulefiles
```

## Load

```bash
module load hpc-setup       # everything
module load bioinf-tools    # bioinformatic tools
module load core-libs       # core libraries
module load terminal-utils  # terminal tools
module load samtools        # a single package
module avail                # list all modules
```

Legacy Nanopore tools (R9.4.1 / fast5 data) are not in the meta-modules:

```bash
module load ont-guppy nanopolish
```

## Terminal tools (Rust)

bat, eza, fd, ripgrep (`rg`), tree and zoxide are built with `cargo install` into
Rust's shared cargo directory, `rust/rust-VERSION/cargo/bin/` (currently
`rust-1.100.0`), not into their own directories. Each still has its own module
file, so it shows up in `module avail` and loads by name. All of these modules
point to the same directory: loading any one of them puts every tool from it
on `PATH`, including `rustc` and `cargo`, and `module load rust` makes the
tools available as well. When Rust is rebuilt or upgraded, the next `boot.sh`
run rebuilds these tools automatically.

```bash
module load bat                 # or eza, fd, ripgrep, tree, zoxide
module load terminal-utils      # all terminal tools, plus git and nvim
FORCE_REBUILD="bat" ./boot.sh   # rebuild one tool by hand
```

## Directory layout

| Path | Content |
|------|---------|
| `NAME/NAME-VERSION/` | installed package |
| `modulefiles/NAME/VERSION.lua` | module files |
| `sources/` | downloaded archives |
| `.stamps/` | finished packages (see [Resume](resume.qmd)) |
| `install.log` | installation log |
